mean: all the ups and downs of life
lit: sour, sweet, bitter and spicy: the four strong flavours

use.how: A noun, usually after 人生的 or 生活中的, or as the object of 尝遍, 经历: 尝遍了人生的酸甜苦辣。

near.diff: 悲欢离合 is the joy and grief of meeting and parting with people; 酸甜苦辣 is every kind of experience, good and hard.

cue: An old man looks back on eighty years: poverty, success, illness, a happy marriage, hard times. He says he has tasted it all.

ctx.s: 生活中的{酸甜苦辣}，只有自己最清楚。
ctx.en: Only you yourself really know the ups and downs of your own life.

ctx.s: 爷爷活了八十多岁，尝遍了人生的{酸甜苦辣}。
ctx.en: Grandpa has lived past eighty and has tasted every flavour of life.

ctx.s: 创业这几年，什么{酸甜苦辣}我都经历过了。
ctx.en: In these years of running my own business I've been through every high and low.

ctx.s: 这本书写出了一个小饭馆老板开店二十年的{酸甜苦辣}。
ctx.en: The book captures all the highs and lows of a small restaurant owner's twenty years in business.

ctx.s: “留学一年感觉怎么样？”“{酸甜苦辣}都有，但我不后悔。”
ctx.en: "How was your year abroad?" "A bit of everything, good and bad, but I don't regret it."

ctx.s: 同学聚会上，大家聊起毕业后各自的{酸甜苦辣}，聊到深夜。
ctx.en: At the reunion everyone talked about their ups and downs since graduation until late at night.

bad.s: 今天我中了奖，真是{酸甜苦辣}！
bad.en: (meant: I won a prize today, how wonderful!)
bad.why: It sums up a mix of good and bad experiences over time, not one happy event.

bad.s: 他{酸甜苦辣}地讲完了自己的经历。
bad.en: (meant: he told his story with mixed feelings)
bad.why: It is a noun for life's experiences, not an adverb describing how someone speaks.

mean: the daily necessities of household life
lit: firewood, rice, oil and salt: what a household buys every day

use.how: A noun for the practical, unromantic side of keeping a home, often 柴米油盐的琐事 or 过日子离不开柴米油盐。

cue: After the honeymoon, a young couple's talk turns to rent, groceries and who pays the electricity bill.

ctx.s: 结婚以后，每天想的都是{柴米油盐}。
ctx.en: After getting married, all you think about every day is the household basics.

ctx.s: 过日子哪能离得开{柴米油盐}？
ctx.en: How can you run a household without thinking about everyday necessities?

ctx.s: 她年轻时爱写诗，现在整天忙着{柴米油盐}的琐事。
ctx.en: She loved writing poetry when she was young; now she's busy all day with household chores and shopping.

ctx.s: 父母一辈子为{柴米油盐}操劳，从来没出过远门。
ctx.en: My parents spent their whole lives toiling over daily necessities and never travelled far.

ctx.s: “你们俩吵什么？”“还不是{柴米油盐}那点事。”
ctx.en: "What are you two arguing about?" "Oh, just the usual household stuff."

ctx.s: 爱情再浪漫，最后也要面对{柴米油盐}。
ctx.en: However romantic love is, in the end it has to face the realities of daily life.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜放了很多{柴米油盐}，太咸了。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant's food has too much seasoning)
bad.why: It stands for the everyday business of running a home, not for the actual seasoning in a dish.

bad.s: 公司今年的{柴米油盐}增加了很多。
bad.en: (meant: the company's operating costs rose a lot)
bad.why: It belongs to family and household life, not to a company's budget or expenses.

lit: to wring out the last of one's brain juice

use.how: A verb phrase, often followed by 也 or a purpose: 绞尽脑汁想办法。It takes no object of its own.

cue: You have to think of a birthday present for someone who already has everything, and you sit for an hour getting nowhere.

ctx.s: 我{绞尽脑汁}，也想不出该送她什么礼物。
ctx.en: I racked my brains but couldn't think what present to give her.

ctx.s: 为了写好这篇作文，他{绞尽脑汁}想了一个晚上。
ctx.en: To write this essay well he racked his brains all evening.

ctx.s: 这道题我{绞尽脑汁}都没做出来，你会吗？
ctx.en: I racked my brains over this problem and still couldn't solve it. Can you?

ctx.s: 广告公司{绞尽脑汁}，终于想出了一句好口号。
ctx.en: The ad agency racked its brains and finally came up with a good slogan.

ctx.s: “孩子不爱吃蔬菜怎么办？”“我也{绞尽脑汁}了，什么办法都试过。”
ctx.en: "What do you do when your kid won't eat vegetables?" "I've racked my brains too, I've tried everything."

ctx.s: 为了给新店起个好名字，老板{绞尽脑汁}。
ctx.en: The owner racked his brains to find a good name for the new shop.

bad.s: 他{绞尽脑汁}地搬了一下午箱子。
bad.en: (meant: he worked very hard moving boxes all afternoon)
bad.why: It is hard mental effort to think of something, not physical labour.

bad.s: 我{绞尽脑汁}这个问题好几天了。
bad.en: (meant: I've been racking my brains over this problem for days)
bad.why: It takes no direct object; the problem must be linked by a preposition or by a following verb such as 'think'.

use.how: Usually opens a clause in narration, followed by the idea it produced: 他灵机一动，想出了一个办法。

near.diff: 心血来潮 is a sudden whim to do something; 灵机一动 is a sudden clever idea that solves a problem.

cue: Locked out with no key, a girl suddenly remembers the window above the back door is never shut, and that is how she gets in.

ctx.s: 他{灵机一动}，想出了一个好办法。
ctx.en: Suddenly it came to him, and he thought of a good solution.

ctx.s: 雨伞忘带了，我{灵机一动}，把文件夹顶在头上跑回了家。
ctx.en: I'd forgotten my umbrella, so on a sudden inspiration I held my folder over my head and ran home.

ctx.s: 饭店里没有生日蛋糕，服务员{灵机一动}，在面条上插了一根蜡烛。
ctx.en: The restaurant had no birthday cake, so the waiter had a bright idea and stuck a candle in a bowl of noodles.

ctx.s: 听说这个产品是设计师{灵机一动}想出来的？
ctx.en: I hear the designer came up with this product in a flash of inspiration?

ctx.s: 眼看比赛要输了，教练{灵机一动}，换上了一名新队员。
ctx.en: With the game about to be lost, the coach had a sudden idea and sent on a new player.

ctx.s: “你怎么想到这样修的？”“当时{灵机一动}，就试了试。”
ctx.en: "How did you think of fixing it like that?" "It just came to me at the time, so I gave it a try."

bad.s: 他{灵机一动}，花了三个月才想出这个方案。
bad.en: (meant: after careful thought he worked out this plan)
bad.why: It is a sudden idea in a moment, which contradicts months of slow thinking.

bad.s: 他是一个很{灵机一动}的人，反应特别快。
bad.en: (meant: he is a very quick-witted person)
bad.why: It names one sudden idea at one moment, not a personal trait; it cannot take 'very' or describe a person.

mean: grinning cheekily, not taking it seriously
lit: playful skin and a laughing face

use.how: Describes someone grinning and joking when they should be serious, often after 别 or as an adverbial with 地: 别嬉皮笑脸的！

near.diff: 油嘴滑舌 is about glib, flippant talk; 嬉皮笑脸 is about the cheeky grinning face and attitude.

cue: A teacher is scolding a boy for breaking a window, and the boy just keeps grinning at her as if it were a joke.

ctx.s: 别{嬉皮笑脸}的，我在跟你说正经事！
ctx.en: Wipe that grin off your face, I'm talking to you about something serious!

ctx.s: 老师批评他，他还{嬉皮笑脸}地顶嘴。
ctx.en: When the teacher told him off, he still grinned cheekily and talked back.

ctx.s: 你闯了这么大的祸，怎么还{嬉皮笑脸}？
ctx.en: You've caused all this trouble, and you're still grinning about it?

ctx.s: 他一进门就{嬉皮笑脸}地向妈妈要零花钱。
ctx.en: As soon as he came in he started wheedling his mum for pocket money with a cheeky grin.

ctx.s: 拍证件照要严肃一点，别{嬉皮笑脸}的。
ctx.en: You have to look serious for an ID photo, so stop grinning.

ctx.s: 爸爸气得脸都红了，弟弟却还是一副{嬉皮笑脸}的样子。
ctx.en: Dad was red in the face with anger, but my little brother still had that cheeky grin on.

bad.s: 宝宝看到妈妈，{嬉皮笑脸}的，真可爱。
bad.en: (meant: the baby smiled happily when it saw its mother)
bad.why: It criticises cheekiness when one should be serious; it cannot describe a baby's innocent, happy smile.

bad.s: 她有一张{嬉皮笑脸}，大家都很喜欢她。
bad.en: (meant: she has a sweet smiling face that everyone likes)
bad.why: It is not praise and not a noun for a pretty face; it describes a cheeky, unserious attitude.

lit: an oily mouth and a slippery tongue

use.how: Describes a person or their talk as glib, joking and insincere, as a predicate or after 别: 这个人油嘴滑舌的。

near.diff: 花言巧语 is sweet talk meant to deceive; 油嘴滑舌 is glib, cheeky banter that just cannot be trusted or taken seriously.

cue: A salesman answers every serious question with a quip and a wink, and you feel you can't believe a word he says.

ctx.s: 这个人{油嘴滑舌}的，说话一点也不靠谱。
ctx.en: That guy is all glib talk; nothing he says is reliable.

ctx.s: 少跟我{油嘴滑舌}，好好说话，你到底去哪儿了？
ctx.en: Cut the smart talk and speak properly: where did you actually go?

ctx.s: 她不喜欢{油嘴滑舌}的男生，更喜欢踏实的人。
ctx.en: She doesn't like smooth-talking boys; she prefers someone steady and down-to-earth.

ctx.s: 电话里我问他正经问题，他却{油嘴滑舌}，满嘴俏皮话。
ctx.en: On the phone I asked him a serious question, and he just gave me glib quips.

ctx.s: 做销售要会说话，但不能{油嘴滑舌}，否则客户不信任你。
ctx.en: In sales you need to talk well, but you can't be glib, or customers won't trust you.

ctx.s: 别看他平时说话{油嘴滑舌}，关键时刻还挺可靠。
ctx.en: He may talk all glib banter day to day, but when it counts he's quite dependable.

bad.s: 他{油嘴滑舌}，口才很好，在辩论赛上拿了第一。
bad.en: (meant: he is very eloquent and won the debate)
bad.why: It criticises flippant, insincere talk; it is never praise for real eloquence in a debate.

bad.s: 这道菜太油了，吃完我{油嘴滑舌}的。
bad.en: (meant: the dish was so greasy my mouth felt oily)
bad.why: It is only used figuratively about a way of talking, never about food or a greasy mouth.

lit: an air of joy spreading far and wide

use.how: Describes people's faces or a whole place full of joy over a happy occasion, as a predicate or with 地 and 的: 家家户户喜气洋洋。

near.diff: 兴高采烈 is lively excitement about doing something; 喜气洋洋 is the happy glow of a celebration or good news, often of a whole place.

cue: On New Year's Eve the whole village is hung with red lanterns and every family is laughing and setting off firecrackers.

ctx.s: 春节到了，家家户户{喜气洋洋}。
ctx.en: Spring Festival has arrived and every household is full of festive cheer.

ctx.s: 婚礼现场布置得{喜气洋洋}的，到处都是红色。
ctx.en: The wedding venue was decorated in festive style, with red everywhere.

ctx.s: 女儿考上了大学，家里一下子{喜气洋洋}的。
ctx.en: Our daughter got into university, and suddenly the whole house was full of joy.

ctx.s: 丰收以后，村子里到处{喜气洋洋}。
ctx.en: After the bumper harvest, the whole village was full of festive cheer.

ctx.s: 今天办公室里怎么{喜气洋洋}的？有什么喜事吗？
ctx.en: Why is the office so full of cheer today? Is there something to celebrate?

ctx.s: 球队夺冠的消息传来，整个城市{喜气洋洋}。
ctx.en: When the news of the team's championship came, the whole city was in a festive mood.

bad.s: 他每天下班回家，{喜气洋洋}地躺在沙发上看电视。
bad.en: (meant: every day after work he relaxes contentedly on the sofa)
bad.why: It describes the joy of a happy occasion or good news, not ordinary daily relaxation.

bad.s: 大家都很{喜气洋洋}这个好消息。
bad.en: (meant: everyone is delighted about the good news)
bad.why: It takes no object and is not modified by 'very'; the cause goes in a separate clause before it.

lit: making sounds of 'ai' and heaving sighs

use.how: A verb phrase for audible sighing out of worry or gloom, often criticised: 别整天唉声叹气的。Takes no object.

near.diff: 垂头丧气 is a dejected look, head hanging; 唉声叹气 is the audible sighing and complaining.

cue: Your flatmate keeps letting out long, heavy sighs at his desk, over and over, and you finally ask what's wrong.

ctx.s: 别整天{唉声叹气}的，事情总会解决的。
ctx.en: Stop sighing all day long; it'll get sorted out eventually.

ctx.s: 他一边看工资单，一边{唉声叹气}。
ctx.en: He kept sighing as he looked at his payslip.

ctx.s: 你从早上起就{唉声叹气}，到底出什么事了？
ctx.en: You've been sighing since this morning. What on earth has happened?

ctx.s: {唉声叹气}解决不了问题，不如想想办法。
ctx.en: Sighing won't solve anything; better to think of a way out.

ctx.s: 奶奶听说菜价又涨了，忍不住{唉声叹气}起来。
ctx.en: When Grandma heard vegetable prices had gone up again, she couldn't help sighing and grumbling.

ctx.s: 考试成绩出来以后，教室里一片{唉声叹气}。
ctx.en: When the exam results came out, the classroom was filled with sighs.

bad.s: 听到这个好消息，他高兴得{唉声叹气}。
bad.en: (meant: he was so happy he gave a sigh of relief)
bad.why: It expresses worry or gloom, never happiness; a sigh of relief is a different expression.

bad.s: 他一直在{唉声叹气}自己的工作。
bad.en: (meant: he keeps moaning about his job)
bad.why: It takes no object; the cause must come before it, after a preposition or in a separate clause.

use.how: As a predicate (结果出乎意料), an attributive with 的, an adverbial with 地 (出乎意料地好), or opening 出乎意料的是。

cue: Everyone was sure the favourite would win the final easily, but an unknown newcomer beat him in straight sets.

ctx.s: 比赛的结果{出乎意料}。
ctx.en: The result of the match was unexpected.

ctx.s: 这家小店的菜{出乎意料}地好吃。
ctx.en: The food at this little place was surprisingly good.

ctx.s: {出乎意料}的是，平时最安静的她第一个举了手。
ctx.en: Unexpectedly, she, usually the quietest, was the first to raise her hand.

ctx.s: 新手机的销量{出乎意料}，连公司自己都没想到。
ctx.en: Sales of the new phone were beyond expectations; even the company hadn't seen it coming.

ctx.s: “面试顺利吗？”“{出乎意料}地顺利，他们当场就录用了我。”
ctx.en: "Did the interview go well?" "Surprisingly well, they hired me on the spot."

ctx.s: 我以为他会生气，没想到他的反应这么平静，真是{出乎意料}。
ctx.en: I thought he'd be angry, but he reacted so calmly. It was a real surprise.

bad.s: 天气预报说今天下雨，果然{出乎意料}地下雨了。
bad.en: (meant: as forecast, it rained)
bad.why: It means against expectations, but 'as expected' in the same sentence says the opposite.

bad.s: 这个结果{出乎意料}了我。
bad.en: (meant: this result surprised me)
bad.why: It takes no object; to name the person surprised, 'my' goes inside it, between its two halves.

lit: to guard against the one chance in ten thousand

use.how: Usually after a clause stating a precaution, or after 为了: 多带点钱，以防万一。It does not take a clause of its own.

near.diff: 有备无患 states the principle that preparation removes worry; 以防万一 explains one specific small precaution.
未雨绸缪 is planning well ahead for future trouble, more formal; 以防万一 is an everyday small precaution.

cue: The sky is clear, but before leaving you still slip a small umbrella into your bag. Why bother?

ctx.s: 今天可能下雨，带把伞吧，{以防万一}。
ctx.en: It might rain today; take an umbrella, just in case.

ctx.s: 我又把文件备份了一份，{以防万一}。
ctx.en: I made another backup of the file, just in case.

ctx.s: 为了{以防万一}，出国前最好买一份旅游保险。
ctx.en: To be on the safe side, it's best to buy travel insurance before going abroad.

ctx.s: “路这么近，还用开导航吗？”“开着吧，{以防万一}。”
ctx.en: "It's so close, do we really need the satnav?" "Keep it on, just in case."

ctx.s: 医生让他在家里备点药，{以防万一}。
ctx.en: The doctor told him to keep some medicine at home, just in case.

ctx.s: 虽然准备得很充分，他还是多打印了几份讲稿，{以防万一}。
ctx.en: Although he was well prepared, he still printed a few extra copies of his speech, just in case.

bad.s: {以防万一}他不来，我们怎么办？
bad.en: (meant: what if he doesn't come, what do we do?)
bad.why: It names a precaution taken just in case; to ask 'what if', the plain word for 'in case' is used alone, not this idiom.

bad.s: 他昨天摔倒了，{以防万一}。
bad.en: (meant: he fell over yesterday, unfortunately)
bad.why: It explains a precaution taken before something might happen, not an accident that already did.
